findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_scripture_for, learn_the_faith, find_churches, find_communities, see_the_kingdom, start_with_christ, search, fetch · Private data: learn_the_faith, find_churches, find_people_to_pray_with, find_communities, start_with_christ · Public sink: discover_living_bread, find_churches, find_people_to_pray_with, see_the_kingdom, start_with_christ · Destructive: start_with_christ.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_scripture_for, learn_the_faith, find_churches, find_communities, see_the_kingdom, start_with_christ, search, fetch · Private data: learn_the_faith, find_churches, find_people_to_pray_with, find_communities, start_with_christ · Public sink: discover_living_bread, find_churches, find_people_to_pray_with, see_the_kingdom, start_with_christ · Destructive: start_with_christ

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
